info.title: OpenStudyBuilder Standards Import API
info.description:
## Purpose

Ingests CDISC controlled terminology packages into the OpenStudyBuilder MDR database.

A CDISC quarterly release is a set of catalogue files sharing one effective date.
Files are uploaded one at a time, but grouping and inconsistency detection run across
all catalogues of the same effective date — so the effective date, not the file, is
the unit of work.

Uploaded files land in a staging database where they are grouped by concept id and
checked for inconsistencies between catalogues. Nothing reaches the MDR database until
the effective date has been analysed and any open review items resolved.

get.summary: Returns 200 OK if the standards-import service is ready to serve requests

post.summary: Upload one CDISC controlled terminology package file
post.description:
Accepts a single CDISC Library controlled terminology package JSON
document — one catalogue at one effective date — and loads it into the staging database.

The catalogue name and effective date are read from the document itself, not from a
filename, so the payload is self-describing.

Uploading is idempotent: re-sending identical bytes for a catalogue and effective date
already staged returns the existing record untouched. Sending different content for the
same catalogue and effective date replaces what was staged, and resets that effective
date to `FILES_STAGED` so it must be analysed again.

A release usually spans several catalogues. Upload each of its files, then run the
analysis for the effective date they share.

get.summary: Count the changes each staged catalogue of a release brings
get.description:
One entry per catalogue staged under this effective date, holding the
same severity bands `GET /packages/files/{catalogue}/diff` returns but counted rather
than listed.

Meant for showing a reviewer where to look before they open anything: a release spans
several catalogues, each full diff runs to many thousands of changes, and asking for all
of them at once to count them is not reasonable.

This is cheaper to send and to consume, not cheaper to compute — each catalogue is still
compared against its predecessor in full. What it saves is carrying every change back and
matching a changelog onto it.

A catalogue whose predecessor is not staged is reported with `previous_available` false
and no bands, rather than left out — the caller can then say so for that catalogue
instead of appearing to have fewer of them than were uploaded.

get.summary: Find which release a diff of this package would compare against
get.description:
Resolves the `HAS_PRIOR_VERSION` link for this catalogue without
computing a diff, so a caller can show what it is about to compare against before the
heavier diff call — which walks every codelist and term of both catalogues — returns.

`previous_available` is `false` when this is the first staged release of the catalogue,
or when its predecessor was never staged — the diff endpoint then returns no bands
either, rather than failing.

get.summary: Diff one staged package against the previous release of its catalogue
get.description:
Compares a staged catalogue against the release it supersedes, banding
every change by how disruptive it could be to an import already done.

The previous release is found via the `HAS_PRIOR_VERSION` link recorded at upload time.
If it is not staged — the first release of this catalogue, or its predecessor was never
uploaded — `previous_available` is `false` and no bands are returned; this is not an
error.

Where a terminology-changes spreadsheet has been uploaded for the release, each change
also carries a `changelog` array holding what CDISC published about it — request codes,
its own change summary, and any implementation instructions. This is annotation only: it
cannot change which changes are found or how they are banded, and a release with no
changelog, or one whose sheet does not mention a given change, returns the same diff it
otherwise would.

Nothing here is persisted: the diff is recomputed from the two catalogues' staged
content on every call.

get.summary: One codelist or term across the last releases of its catalogue
get.description:
Lays the attributes of one codelist or term side by side across the
releases of a catalogue leading up to `effective_date`, which is the last of them — the
release under review. The chain follows the `HAS_PRIOR_VERSION` links recorded at upload
time, so it is shorter than `releases` where an earlier release was never staged; the
first release then has `is_earliest_staged` set.

A release that does not hold the concept is still listed, with `present` false and null
values. For a term, `membership_changes` also gives the codelists it entered and left in
each release against the one before; the codelists it stayed in are not listed. A term's
`submissionValue` is the value it has in the codelists holding it, joined when they
differ.

`404` when the catalogue is not staged for that date, or when none of the releases
holds the concept. Nothing here is persisted.

post.summary: Find out which CDISC releases have been published since the last one known
post.description:
Reads the CDISC Library's package list and reports the releases staging
has not heard of yet, so a new quarterly release does not have to be noticed by hand.
Returns immediately with a job to follow; `GET /jobs/{uid}` reports what it found in
`stats` once it finishes — `new_release_count`, `skipped_count`, `auto_staged_count`.

A release is one effective date, the same thing shown first in the releases table — not
a catalogue. New means newer, strictly: a published package counts only if its effective
date is later than the newest one staging holds *at all*, whether that one was uploaded
or reported by an earlier call here. A release at or before that date is not reported,
because loading it would mean rewriting history, which is the bootstrap import's job
rather than this app's.

For most catalogues, no content is fetched — what the job finds is a list of releases
worth uploading, each with the path CDISC publishes it under; uploading the package files
is still a separate, deliberate step. **SDTM CT is the exception**: its content is fetched
from CDISC and staged the same way a manual upload would be. If the fetch or the staging
fails, the release is still reported — every other catalogue and release found in the
same run is unaffected. Calling this twice in a row therefore reports the releases once
and then nothing — it records what it found, and that is the only thing it writes.

Published entries whose name does not end with an effective date cannot be placed under a
catalogue and are counted rather than failing the run.

Needs `STANDARDS_IMPORT_CDISC_API_BASE_URL` to be configured; without it the call is
refused immediately rather than starting a job that could only fail, which would be
indistinguishable from CDISC having published nothing new. Refused as well while another
discovery run is already in progress — there is one at a time, not one per release.

The caller supplies their own CDISC Library API key in the request body. It is held in
memory for the duration of the run and nowhere else: not in configuration, not on the
job, not in the response.

post.summary: Upload a paired-codelist workbook for this release
post.description:
Records which code codelist each name codelist belongs with, from the
paired-view spreadsheet CDISC publishes alongside the packages.

This cannot be reliably derived from the packages themselves — the submission values
usually imply the pairing, but not always — so the workbook has to be uploaded with the
release, the same way the package files are. One per catalogue family (SDTM, SEND, ADaM);
each replaces only its own previous upload, so they do not overwrite each other.

Send the `.xlsx` as the raw request body and name it with `source_file`. Rows that are
not a name/code pair are passed over and listed back to you rather than failing the
upload.

Upload the packages first: the pairings attach to the release they belong to. Analyse
afterwards, which is what turns these into review items.

post.summary: Upload a terminology-changes spreadsheet for this release
post.description:
Records what CDISC says it changed in one catalogue this release,
from the terminology-changes spreadsheet published alongside the packages.

**This is informational and changes nothing about the release.** It does not feed the
analysis, does not raise or settle review items, and does not affect whether the release
can be imported. Unlike a package or pairing upload it leaves the release's status
alone, so uploading one against an `ANALYZED` release does not send it back to
`FILES_STAGED` — and a release that has already been imported still accepts one.

Each row is attached to the codelist or term it is about, so the notes show up against
that codelist in `GET /effective-dates/{date}/codelists/{codelist_id}`. Upload the
catalogue's package file first: without it there is nothing to attach to, and the upload
is refused. Rows about a codelist retired in this release have no codelist left to hang
on and attach to the catalogue instead — `GET /effective-dates/{date}/changelog` is
where those are read.

The catalogue is taken from the sheet title, so one file describes one catalogue and
re-uploading it replaces that catalogue's entries without touching the others. Pass
`catalogue` to override it if CDISC ever titles a sheet differently.

Send the `.xls` as the raw request body and name it with `source_file`. CDISC publishes
these in the legacy binary `.xls` format; an `.xlsx` re-saved from one is not read.

post.summary: Group and check one CDISC release
post.description:
Groups the staged catalogue files of this effective date by concept id
and raises a review item wherever the catalogues disagree. Returns immediately with a
job to follow; the release's status is `ANALYZING` until it finishes, then `ANALYZED`
or `BLOCKED`. `GET /effective-dates/{effective_date}/analysis` reads the outcome once
it has — or `GET /jobs/{uid}` to follow the job itself.

Call this once every file of the release has been uploaded — a release analysed while
files are still missing will be grouped against an incomplete set of catalogues.

Re-running is safe and is how you re-check after resolving review items: earlier findings
for this effective date are discarded and derived again from the staged files. Refused
while an import, another analysis, or a sponsor impact assessment of the same release is
already running.

Nothing is written to the MDR database here.

schema.description: Effective date of the release, as `YYYY-MM-DD`
schema.title: Effective Date

get.description:

post.summary: Work out what this release would collide with in the MDR database
post.description:
Compares the release against the codelists and terms the sponsor has
defined, and raises a review item for each collision. Writes nothing to the MDR database.
Returns immediately with a job to follow; the release's status is `ASSESSING` until it
finishes. `GET /effective-dates/{effective_date}/sponsor-impact` reads the outcome once
it has — or `GET /jobs/{uid}` to follow the job itself.

Three things are reported: a term this release adds to a codelist that a sponsor-defined
term in the same codelist already covers, a codelist it introduces that a sponsor codelist
already covers, and a term whose sponsor name is no longer what the naming rules would
produce now that CDISC has changed it.

The findings join the same review queue as CDISC inconsistencies and are settled through
`POST /inconsistencies/{uid}/resolution`. Most are settled automatically by the shipped
rules; an **exact** collision on a term is not, because that is the one that breaks a
uniqueness rule the main API enforces, and somebody has to say what to do about it — even
if what they say is to keep both.

Run this after the preview and before the import. It needs an analysed release with
nothing else open, because what a term collides with depends on the name the review items
settled for it. Re-running is safe: decisions already made are kept and reattached, and
are discarded only if the values they were made about have changed. Refused while an
import, an analysis, or another assessment of the same release is already running.

schema.description: Effective date of the release, as `YYYY-MM-DD`
schema.title: Effective Date

Not normally needed: an answer is only reused where the question is identical, so a codelist whose settled names have moved is asked again on its own. This is for when the answers rather than the inputs have changed — a new model, or a provider pointed elsewhere.

get.summary: See what importing this release would change
get.description:
Compares the release against what the OSB database currently holds and
reports what the import would create, what it would version, and what it would leave
alone. Writes nothing.

`can_import` and `blockers` say whether the import would be accepted and, if not, why —
so this is also the way to check a release is ready without attempting it.

post.summary: Import this release into the OSB database
post.description:
Applies the release and returns immediately with a job to follow.

The import is **append-only at the head**: it extends what OSB already holds with one
newer release. A release older than the newest package already there is refused, because
loading it would mean rewriting history — that is the bootstrap import's job, run once
per environment.

Refused as well if anything is still open for review, if the release has already been
imported, or if a job for it is already running. Pass `expected_catalogues` to assert the
release holds exactly the catalogues you think it does: a half-uploaded release would
otherwise import quietly, and its missing catalogues could never be added afterwards.

Concepts whose values are unchanged get no new version — only what CDISC actually
changed is versioned.

post.description:
Records how this disagreement should be settled, and what value that
produces. The value is applied to the grouped concept by the next analysis run.

Set `save_as_rule` to also store the choice as a standing rule, so the same
disagreement is settled automatically next quarter instead of coming back. `rule_scope`
decides how widely that rule reaches — from this one concept and property at this one
release, up to every finding of this kind.

Re-analysis keeps the decision, unless the competing values themselves have changed:
a decision made about different values is discarded rather than silently reapplied.

parameters.name: uid

schema.description: Uid of the review item
schema.title: Uid

parameters.description: Uid of the review item

delete.description:
Removes the decision and puts the item back in the queue.

Any rule saved alongside the original decision is left alone — delete it separately if
the whole standing choice was a mistake, otherwise the next analysis run will simply
settle this item the same way again.

parameters.name: uid

schema.description: Uid of the review item
schema.title: Uid

get.summary: Which strategies settle which kind of review item
get.description:
The menu behind `POST /inconsistencies/{uid}/resolution`: for every kind
of review item, the strategies that can settle it, and for every strategy what it needs
to be given and whether a decision using it may be saved as a rule.

This is the same table the resolution endpoint enforces, so a client that offers exactly
what is listed here will never be refused on the kind of finding alone. It is the first
gate, not the last: a listed strategy can still refuse a particular finding — one value
to accept where there are two, a catalogue that supplied nothing — and says why.

Each kind's list has the usual choice first. That is the only opinion it carries.

`raised_by` says which step raises each kind: `ANALYSIS`
(`POST /effective-dates/{date}/analysis`) or `SPONSOR_IMPACT`
(`POST /effective-dates/{date}/sponsor-impact`). Every `ANALYSIS` kind has to be settled,
and the release re-analysed, before sponsor impact can even be assessed — this is a fixed
property of the kind, not something that varies finding to finding, so it is safe to use
for splitting a queue into two lists before any of it is fetched.

get.summary: List resolution rules
get.description:
Returns the standing decisions, narrowest first — which is the order
analysis matches them in, so the first rule that applies to a finding is the one that
settles it.

schema.title: Response Get Resolution Rules Resolution Rules Get

post.description:
Stores a standing decision.

A rule constrains only the fields it sets and ignores the rest, so `scope` has to pin
down what it claims to — a `CONCEPT` rule without a `concept_id` would quietly apply
everywhere, and is rejected.

The uid is composed from what the rule discriminates on, so saving the same rule twice
updates it rather than stacking a duplicate that would compete with itself.

patch.description:
Changes what a rule does, most usefully `enabled`.

Disabling a rule is how you take a standing decision out of service without losing the
record of it — the seeded rule that names every new term after its CDISC preferred term,
for instance, can be switched off so each one is reviewed by hand instead.

What the rule *matches on* is fixed: those fields compose its uid, so changing them
would be a different rule. Create that one instead.

Takes effect at the next analysis run; decisions already made are not revisited.

get.summary: Get the catalogue pecking order
get.description:
The fallback used when catalogues disagree over a value and no rule
applies: the most authoritative catalogue that supplied a value wins.

This is what settles the great majority of disagreements, and matches what the bootstrap
import script does — the difference being that here the order is data you can read and
change rather than a list in Python.

schema.title: Response Get Catalogue Priority Config Catalogue Priority Get

put.description:
Replaces the order wholesale, so a catalogue left out of the list is
genuinely removed from it.

Takes effect at the next analysis run. Decisions already made are not revisited.

schema.title: Response Set Catalogue Priority Config Catalogue Priority Put

put.description:
Sets which catalogues a release must hold before it can be
analysed — read together with the rest of the pecking order on
`GET /config/catalogue-priority`, under `mandatory`.

Replaces the set wholesale, so a catalogue left out is no longer mandatory. Every name
must already appear in the catalogue pecking order; add it there first.

Takes effect on the next `POST /effective-dates/{date}/analysis` — a release missing
one of these is refused, naming what is missing.

schema.title: Response Set Mandatory Catalogues Config Mandatory Catalogues Put

put.summary: Replace the catalogues expected to ship a workbook
put.description:
Sets which catalogues usually ship a paired-view workbook alongside
their package files — read together with the rest of the pecking order on
`GET /config/catalogue-priority`, under `expects_workbook`.

Informational only: a workbook is not always published, so this never gates analysis
or import. It exists to be shown to whoever is uploading a release, alongside the
pairing-workbook table.

Replaces the set wholesale. Every name must already appear in the catalogue pecking
order; add it there first.

`InconsistencyStatus`, `RuleScope` and `EffectiveDateStatus` value means, for tooltips
and help text around the review screens — `SPONSOR_TERM_SEMANTIC_DUPLICATE` is no
clearer to a reviewer than it is to a newcomer to this codebase.

missed — a plain lifecycle step like `EffectiveDateStatus.IMPORTING` speaks for itself.

get.description:
One call for what `/preview`, `/inconsistencies` and the review
progress would otherwise take several to assemble: release-wide change counts, review
items broken down by status and by which pass raised them, and how many of the
codelists worth a look have been marked reviewed.

Nothing here is new data — it is the same numbers `/preview` and `/inconsistencies`
already report, regrouped for a first screen. Settling something specific is still
faster through those endpoints or through `/effective-dates/{effective_date}/codelists`.

get.description:
Regroups the release-wide change counts and review items by the
codelist they belong to, so a reviewer can work through the release codelist by

still to acknowledge, then the rest; each group is ordered by codelist id.

get.summary: One row per term this release touches
get.description:
The term-side counterpart of `/codelists`: the same release regrouped
by term rather than by the codelist holding it, for a reviewer working through what
changed about the terms themselves.

Only terms the release **changes** are returned — new, changed, gaining or losing a
codelist, or gone from the release. A term it leaves alone is never listed, not even when
it carries a finding: that finding still counts against its codelist in `/codelists`.

A term reported `DELETED` has left every codelist this release ships; it is not deleted
from the MDR, which has no way to delete a term at all. `review_status` is inherited from
the codelists holding the term — there is no per-term review mark to set.

Two things deliberately absent from a term's row: `INCONSISTENT_TERM_SETS` is about which
terms a codelist contains rather than about any one of them, so it counts against the
codelist only; and a term's sponsor name is never rewritten by a release, so `name` is
not among the impacted properties — a name in dispute is a `SPONSOR_NAME` or
`SPONSOR_NAME_DIVERGED` finding instead.

get.summary: What this release changes on one term, in every codelist holding it
get.description:
The term-side counterpart of `/codelists/{codelist_id}`: what changed
on the term itself, and each codelist holding it — once this release lands, or until it
does — with the term's submission value there, whether the release opens or closes that
membership, and the findings keyed on that pair.

Findings about the term itself are listed once, at the top level, rather than repeated
under every codelist. Each is the same `Inconsistency` object the flat review queue
returns, settled the same way.

Unlike `/terms`, any term the release ships can be read here, changed or not, and so can
a term it no longer ships while MDR still holds it in one of the release's codelists.
`review` is inherited from those codelists — there is no per-term review mark to set.

Records that a person has looked at this codelist — refused while
anything on it is still OPEN, checked against the same `show=all` view the detail
endpoint returns, not the default filtered one, so nothing hiding behind `show=changed`
can be reviewed past unseen.

Never blocks `POST /effective-dates/{effective_date}/import` — this is a progress aid,
and import stays gated purely by open findings, exactly as before this existed.

Reviewing an already-reviewed codelist again refreshes who and when. If a later
analysis reopens a finding on it, the status flips to `REVIEWED_STALE` on its own —
the record of this review is kept, not deleted; mark it again once the new finding
is settled.

would show a reviewer the same sentence two or three times with nothing visibly

not only with themselves: analysis rebuilds the same grouped layer assessment
reads and import writes from, so any two running at once on the same release
would race. Uploads and review-item resolutions are refused during all three
for the same reason.

MatchTier.title: MatchTier
MatchTier.description:
How closely a CDISC value and a sponsor-defined one agree.

The tiers are not degrees of tidiness; they separate a broken invariant from a
judgement call. Only `EXACT` breaks something the main API enforces — a term's name
must be unique among the terms of the codelists it belongs to, and a codelist's name
and submission value are unique outright. Nothing in this app's Cypher stops an exact
collision, so it imports silently and leaves MDR in a state the main API then refuses
to edit. The other two break nothing at all: they mean two things end up meaning the
same under different spellings, which is for a person to weigh.

Which release, if any, a catalogue's diff would be compared against.

Split out from `PackageDiffReport` so the frontend can show which release it is
comparing against before the full diff — which walks every codelist and term of
both catalogues — has finished computing.

ReleaseDashboard.title: ReleaseDashboard
ReleaseDashboard.description: Overview of one release: what changed, what's outstanding, review progress.

assessed_at.description: Null if sponsor impact has never been assessed

ReleaseInconsistencyStats.description: Review items of one release, split by which pass raised them.

in_scope.description: Codelists worth a look: changed, or carrying a finding

stale.title: Stale
stale.description: Reviewed, then reopened by a later analysis; see `REVIEWED_STALE`

ReleaseReviewStats.title: ReleaseReviewStats
ReleaseReviewStats.description: How far the codelist-by-codelist walkthrough has got. Never blocks import.

resolved_value.title: Resolved Value
resolved_value.description: The value that analysis will apply to the grouped concept

rule_uid.title: Rule Uid
rule_uid.description: Set when a stored rule made this decision rather than a person

ResolutionDecision.title: ResolutionDecision
ResolutionDecision.description: The decision that settled a review item.

save_as_rule.title: Save As Rule
save_as_rule.description: Also store this as a rule, so the same disagreement is settled automatically next time instead of coming back

rule_scope.description: How widely the saved rule should apply

ResolutionInput.title: ResolutionInput
ResolutionInput.description: A reviewer settling one review item.

strategies.title: Strategies
strategies.description: Every strategy, with what it needs and what it does

by_type.title: By Type
by_type.description: For each kind of review item, the strategies that can settle it, the usual choice first. Where the menu depends on `match_tier` this is the one for a finding with no tier or an `EXACT` one — the most restrictive; `by_type_and_tier` has the rest

by_type_and_tier.title: By Type And Tier
by_type_and_tier.description: For the kinds whose menu depends on `match_tier`, the menu at each tier. A kind absent here has one menu at every tier. `ACKNOWLEDGE` is only offered where the finding does not block import

raised_by.title: Raised By
raised_by.description: For each kind of review item, which step raises it — `ANALYSIS` (`POST /effective-dates/{date}/analysis`) or `SPONSOR_IMPACT` (`POST /effective-dates/{date}/sponsor-impact`). Every `ANALYSIS` kind must be settled, and the release re-analysed, before sponsor impact can run at all — this is a fixed property of the kind, not of any one finding

ResolutionOptions.title: ResolutionOptions
ResolutionOptions.description:
Which strategies settle which kind of review item.

The same table `POST /inconsistencies/{uid}/resolution` enforces, so what a client
offers and what the endpoint accepts cannot drift. Admissible on kind is the first
gate, not the last: a listed strategy can still refuse a particular finding — one
value to accept where there are two, a catalogue that supplied nothing — and says so.

effective_date.title: Effective Date
effective_date.description: Limits the rule to one release; unset means every release

match_tier.description: Matches only findings whose colliding values agree this closely. This is how a rule can wave through near-matches while leaving exact ones for a person, since only those break a uniqueness rule

related_concept_id.title: Related Concept Id
related_concept_id.description: Matches only the finding about this term. Needed where the term is not the concept: a submission value belongs to the membership, so those findings carry the codelist as `concept_id` and the term here

in_codelist_id.title: In Codelist Id
in_codelist_id.description: Matches a term that belongs to this codelist. Unlike the other discriminators this is a membership test, which is how a rule reaches every term of a codelist without naming them

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: The ordered substitutions a REWRITE applies

when.title: When
when.description: Regular expression the value must match for this rule to apply. Lets a narrow conditional rule sit in front of a broader one for the same codelist, which is how `Administration via …` is treated differently from the rest of its codelist.

title_case.title: Title Case
title_case.description: Title-case the result, for values taken from a submission value

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Order among equally scoped rules; lower is tried first

ResolutionRule.title: ResolutionRule
ResolutionRule.description: A standing decision, applied by analysis without asking.

match_tier.description: Matches only findings whose colliding values agree this closely

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: The ordered substitutions a REWRITE applies

when.title: When
when.description: Regular expression the value must match for this rule to apply. Lets a narrow conditional rule sit in front of a broader one for the same codelist, which is how `Administration via …` is treated differently from the rest of its codelist.

priority.title: Priority

ResolutionRuleUpdate.title: ResolutionRuleUpdate
ResolutionRuleUpdate.description:
Changes to a stored rule.

Only what the rule *does* can change. What it matches on composes its uid, so
altering that would make it a different rule.

ResolutionStrategy.title: ResolutionStrategy
ResolutionStrategy.description: How a review item is settled, and what value that produces.

ReviewPass.title: ReviewPass
ReviewPass.description:
Which step raises a kind of review item.

A finding's kind is fixed at the moment it exists, so this is really a property of
`InconsistencyType` rather than of any one finding — every `SPONSOR_NAME` is
`ANALYSIS`, every `SPONSOR_NAME_DIVERGED` is `SPONSOR_IMPACT`, with no exceptions.
`ANALYSIS` types must be settled, and the release re-analysed, before
`POST /effective-dates/{date}/sponsor-impact` can run at all — see
`guard_assessable` and "What it compares" in the README.

ReviewStatus.title: ReviewStatus
ReviewStatus.description: Where a codelist stands in the review walkthrough. Never blocks import.

replacement.title: Replacement
replacement.description: What to put in its place

RewriteStep.title: RewriteStep
RewriteStep.description: One substitution in a `REWRITE`, applied in the order listed.

RuleScope.title: RuleScope
RuleScope.description: How widely a rule applies. Narrower scopes win when several rules match.

findings.title: Findings
findings.description: What the assessment raised, by kind and how it stands

open_finding_count.title: Open Finding Count
open_finding_count.description: Sponsor impact findings still to be settled. Import is blocked while this is above zero

by_match_tier.title: By Match Tier
by_match_tier.description: Collisions by how closely the values agree. Only `EXACT` breaks a uniqueness rule the main API enforces, and only those are left open by the shipped rules

checked_codelists.title: Checked Codelists
checked_codelists.description: Codelists this release introduces that were compared against every sponsor-defined codelist

checked_memberships.title: Checked Memberships
checked_memberships.description: Terms this release adds to a codelist that already holds sponsor-defined terms, each compared against them. A count of zero with no findings means nothing was comparable, not that nothing collides

checked_semantically.title: Checked Semantically
checked_semantically.description: Terms a language model was asked about, having found no string match. Zero means the question was never put — either no provider is configured or the strings had already answered for every addition — which is not the same as nothing being found

checked_updated_terms.title: Checked Updated Terms
checked_updated_terms.description: Terms this release changes whose name in MDR was compared against what the naming rules would produce today

checked_removed_or_changed_terms.title: Checked Removed Or Changed Terms
checked_removed_or_changed_terms.description: Terms this release changes the submission value of, or takes out of a codelist, checked against the MDR database for a downstream reference. A finding is raised only for the ones that have one — a count here with no matching finding means the rest were unreferenced, not that nothing was checked

SponsorImpactSummary.title: SponsorImpactSummary
SponsorImpactSummary.description: What this release would mean for the sponsor-defined content already in MDR.

catalogue.title: Catalogue
catalogue.description: Catalogue the sheet title named, or the `catalogue` query parameter where one was given

source_file.title: Source File
source_file.description: Name you gave the uploaded spreadsheet

sheet.title: Sheet
sheet.description: Sheet the rows were read from

collapsed.title: Collapsed
collapsed.description: Rows folded into an entry already counted. CDISC repeats a codelist rename once per member term; those become one entry about the codelist

StagedChangelogFile.title: StagedChangelogFile
StagedChangelogFile.description: A terminology-changes spreadsheet uploaded for a release.

package_name.title: Package Name
package_name.description: Package name as given by CDISC, for example `SDTM CT 2024-09-27`

effective_date.title: Effective Date
effective_date.description: Effective date of the release this file belongs to

sha256.title: Sha256
sha256.description: Digest of the uploaded bytes, used to detect re-uploads

size_bytes.title: Size Bytes
size_bytes.description: Size of the uploaded file in bytes

codelist_count.title: Codelist Count
codelist_count.description: Number of codelists found in the file

term_count.title: Term Count
term_count.description: Number of term entries found in the file

replaced_previous_upload.title: Replaced Previous Upload
replaced_previous_upload.description: Whether this upload replaced an earlier one for the same catalogue and effective date

source_file.title: Source File
source_file.description: Name you gave the uploaded workbook

skipped.title: Skipped
skipped.description: Rows that are not a name/code pair and were passed over

StagedPairingFile.title: StagedPairingFile
StagedPairingFile.description: A paired-codelist workbook uploaded for a release.

needs.title: Needs
needs.description: Fields of the resolution this strategy cannot do without — `value`, `catalogue`, `pattern` or `steps`. Anything else it takes is optional and the description says what it is for

can_save_as_rule.title: Can Save As Rule
can_save_as_rule.description: Whether a resolution using it accepts `save_as_rule`. False for the ones that change what the MDR database already holds, which are never standing rules, and for `USE_SUBMISSION_VALUE`, whose rule has to name a codelist a resolution cannot — write that one through `/resolution-rules`

StrategyDescription.title: StrategyDescription
StrategyDescription.description: One way of settling a review item, and what it has to be given.

TermChangeStatus.title: TermChangeStatus
TermChangeStatus.description:
What this release does to one term, across every codelist that holds it.

Distinct from `ChangeStatus`, which a codelist uses: a term can be touched by a
membership change while its own attributes are identical, and it can drop out of the
release altogether — neither of which a codelist does. There is no `UNCHANGED`: a
term the release leaves alone is not listed at all.

term_submission_value.title: Term Submission Value
term_submission_value.description: The term's submission value in this codelist once this release lands. For a membership the release ends, the one MDR holds. Null for a codelist only a finding ties the term to — one a decision took it out of

previous_submission_value.title: Previous Submission Value
previous_submission_value.description: What MDR holds, set only where this release gives the term a different submission value in this codelist

membership_change.description: Set when this release opens or closes this membership

findings.title: Findings
findings.description: Findings about the term inside this codelist: keyed on the codelist, naming the term in `related_concept_id`

TermCodelistMembership.title: TermCodelistMembership
TermCodelistMembership.description: One codelist a term belongs to, seen from the term.

preferred_term.title: Preferred Term
preferred_term.description: What this release calls it. For a term the release no longer ships, what MDR holds

change_status.description: Of the term's own attributes. Null for a term the release no longer ships at all: it is shown only because its memberships close

changes.title: Changes
changes.description: What changed on the term itself. For a NEW term, every attribute it brings, each without an old value. Empty when UNCHANGED

attributes.title: Attributes
attributes.description: Every attribute of the term as this release defines it, or as MDR holds it for a term the release no longer ships

findings.title: Findings
findings.description: Findings about the term itself, wherever it is held

codelists.title: Codelists
codelists.description: Every codelist holding the term once this release lands, plus the ones it is leaving, by codelist id

usage.title: Usage
usage.description: What in the MDR database refers to the term today, read at request time, by kind - the same check the sponsor impact assessment counts for `usage_count`. Empty for a term MDR does not hold yet, or one nothing refers to

changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.description: What CDISC said it changed about this term, in any codelist holding it, where a terminology-changes spreadsheet has been uploaded. Commentary only — nothing here is a finding, and none of it blocks anything

review.description: Inherited from the codelists holding this term, as in `/terms` — there is no per-term review mark

TermDetail.title: TermDetail
TermDetail.description: What one release changes on one term, in every codelist holding it.

total.title: Total
total.description: Matching terms across all pages, not just this one

page_size.title: Page Size
page_size.description: 0 means every matching term was returned on one page

TermPage.title: TermPage
TermPage.description: A page of `GET .../terms`, filtered before it was paginated.

TermScope.title: TermScope
TermScope.description: Which terms a codelist's detail view returns.

preferred_term.title: Preferred Term
preferred_term.description: What this release calls it. For a DELETED term the release says nothing, so this is what MDR holds

impacted.title: Impacted
impacted.description: What the change touches. Empty for NEW

changes.title: Changes
changes.description: Old value beside new, for each impacted property that has one. Nothing for `membership` or `submission_value`, which are per codelist

codelist_count.title: Codelist Count
codelist_count.description: Codelists holding the term once this release lands. Memberships the release ends are not counted, so a DELETED term reports 0

review.description: Inherited from the codelists holding this term — there is no per-term review mark, and nothing here can be marked directly

TermSummary.title: TermSummary
TermSummary.description: One term's change, membership, finding and review state, for the list view.

through.title: Through
through.description: How the reference reaches the term: `selected in context` (through a `CTTermContext` - activity items, unit definitions, ODM items, study selections, template categories) or `used by name` (a syntax instance built on the term's name)

relationship.title: Relationship
relationship.description: The relationship the referring node holds

TermUsage.title: TermUsage
TermUsage.description: One kind of thing in the MDR database that refers to a term, and how many.

BearerJwtAuth.name: Authorization
BearerJwtAuth.description: Access token that will be sent as `Authorization: Bearer {token}` header in all requests
